summary: Full read of 20 SEC whistleblower award orders (2 Aug - 8 Oct 2021); short last pages were also OCRed (no extra content). Adds 11 denial case rows (other claimants and related-action claims denied in the same orders). Suggested corrections add to each existing award row how the claimant qualified, contests, reductions for reporting delay, the 30% presumption, the compliance-role 120-day exception, independent analysis and internal-reporting facts, and fix three data errors: Release 93274 prints "approximately $100,000" but the row has no amount; Release 92621 prints "approximately $3.5 million" whole (note wrongly says no amount / split by a redaction); Release 93016 award_pct should be 30 (joint award). No statistics, new rules or new events.

suggested_corrections.value: Exchange Act Release No. 92542, File No. 2021-77. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Orders (PDF)" (Aug. 2, 2021). Separate award amounts per claimant in one order: this row is the amount stated for Claimant 1 (claimants numbered in the order the amounts appear). Amount as printed: "more than": lower bound. Claimant 1. Not contested. First to tell staff of the conduct at issue ("Issue A"), several months before Claimant 2, establishing the outline of the case; information broader and more current; raised concerns internally repeatedly; telephone interview and documents, though stopped assisting at one point despite staff requests. Presumption criteria discussed for Claimant 1 (no negative factors). Percentage redacted.
Larger share to the first claimant to report the conduct, who had repeatedly raised concerns internally.

Exchange Act Release No. 92542, File No. 2021-77. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Orders (PDF)" (Aug. 2, 2021). Separate award amounts per claimant in one order: this row is the amount stated for Claimant 2 (claimants numbered in the order the amounts appear). Amount as printed: "more than": lower bound. Claimant 2. Contested the split, seeking a larger share; rejected. Reduced for unreasonable reporting delay (about four years after learning of the conduct, with no steps to remedy it; futility of internal reporting and late understanding of illegality rejected). Contributions to a separate covered action against the company ("Issue B") to be considered separately; no credit for charges the SEC could have brought (citing Release No. 90872). Ongoing assistance during the investigation. Percentage redacted.
Smaller share, upheld on reconsideration, for a claimant who waited about four years to report; credit for a separate action left for later.

Exchange Act Release No. 92587, File No. 2021-78. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Aug. 6, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "approximately". Award amount and percentage are as recommended by the Claims Review Staff and adopted by the Commission unless the order says otherwise. Tip about an ongoing fraud prompted the opening of an investigation; multiple voluntary interviews and documents. Footnote 1: a separate action arising from the same facts will be treated as part of the covered action if its sanctions are under $1,000,000 (Rule 21F-4(d)(2)). Percentage redacted; contest status not stated; no other claimants.
Award for a tip about an ongoing fraud that opened the investigation.

Exchange Act Release No. 92767, File No. 2021-84. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Aug. 26, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Claimant, a harmed investor, gave important information on misrepresentations used to induce the investment, which significantly contributed to the action; spoke with staff and gave documents. The order says that because nothing has been collected, the 30% award would not result in any payment. Contest status not stated; no other claimants.
Maximum 30% award under the presumption to a harmed investor; nothing collected, so no payment.

Exchange Act Release No. 92777, File No. 2021-85. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Aug. 27, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "approximately". Award amount and percentage are as recommended by the Claims Review Staff and adopted by the Commission unless the order says otherwise. Outsider credited with "independent analysis" (Rule 21F-4(b)(3)): built and applied a complex algorithm to publicly available data; information early in the investigation significantly contributed (saved time, helped in settlement negotiations with the company); ongoing assistance by phone and email. Related-action claim denied (separate row). Percentage redacted; contest status not stated.
Award for independent analysis: an algorithm applied to public data that helped the investigation and settlement talks; related-action claim denied.

Exchange Act Release No. 92778, File No. 2021-86. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Orders (PDF)" (Aug. 27, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 3. Amount as printed: "over": lower bound. Award amount and percentage are as recommended by the Claims Review Staff and adopted by the Commission unless the order says otherwise. Three claimants, separate (redacted) percentages; awards "collectively" over $1 million, no per-claimant amount printed. None contested. All three held compliance roles but qualified under the 120-day exception (Rule 21F-4(b)): Claimants 1 and 2 waited more than 120 days after reporting internally; Claimant 3 reported over 120 days after learning senior management already knew. Claimant 1: most significant information, extraordinary assistance; Claimant 2: first to report, framework for information requests; Claimant 3: less significant. Claimant 4 denied (separate row).
Awards to three compliance-role insiders, eligible under the 120-day exception after reporting internally first; combined over $1 million.

Exchange Act Release No. 92780, File No. 2021-87. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Aug. 27, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "more than": lower bound. Award amount and percentage are as recommended by the Claims Review Staff and adopted by the Commission unless the order says otherwise. Not contested. Outsider credited with "independent analysis" of public information: identified a microcap company whose stock was the subject of a suspicious promotional campaign, comparing touting emails with other campaigns (expertise built over many years); caused staff to inquire into different conduct in a current investigation (Rule 21F-4(c)(1)); real-time information on the incipient campaign. A related enforcement action will count as part of the covered action if its sanctions are $1 million or less. Percentage redacted; no other claimants.
Award to an outside analyst whose comparison of stock-promotion emails exposed a microcap promotion campaign.

suggested_corrections.value: Exchange Act Release No. 93016, File No. 2021-93. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Sept. 16, 2021).
